# Owned stream inputs

`scripts/generate-stream-fixtures.py` creates these small test inputs from project-owned byte patterns using Python's reference BZip2/LZMA implementations. `--check` checks reproducibility. Phrase inputs contain `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times. Empty members contain no bytes. `multiple.bz2` concatenates an empty and phrase member; `multiple.lz` concatenates phrase, empty and phrase members. The multiblock input contains 320,000 bytes defined by `(i * 73 ^ (i >> 8)) & 255` and uses BZip2 level 1.

TAR inputs contain one `hello.txt` with the phrase, represented as deterministic ustar with a zero timestamp. The LZMA Alone known-size vector patches only the eight-byte size field of the independent unknown-size stream, retaining its EOS marker. Lzip v1 framing follows the [author's format description](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-diaz-lzip/02/), using independently generated raw LZMA and Python's CRC32. This generator is not itself an independent Lzip interoperability result; actual external-reader results belong in the delivery issue. The `bad-header` inputs keep valid compression framing and a ustar marker, but deliberately change the first name byte without updating the TAR header checksum. They verify that identified TAR corruption cannot downgrade to ordinary-file success. No reference implementation code, user archives or execution evidence is stored here.

`scripts/generate-xz-fixtures.py --xz <reference-xz>` generates XZ inputs using Python/liblzma and the official XZ Utils 5.8.4 binary for ARM64, RISC-V and padded-stream verification. The pinned Windows ZIP is from the author's [release](https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz/releases/tag/v5.8.4), SHA-256 `f31af7638391ecf286d48bc8555ce6e131691a1c52a9e44303bce57069e9de56`; reference tools remain under local `build/toolchain/`. `--check` compares the regenerated bytes. Phrase vectors cover None/CRC32/CRC64/SHA-256; `multiple.xz` concatenates phrase, empty and phrase streams with zero padding. `multiblock.xz` combines two independent blocks and is decoded independently before writing. Filter inputs repeat the script's fixed 40-byte instruction pattern 300 times, covering all eight BCJ forms, Delta distance 256 and a Delta/x86 chain. TAR inputs preserve the owned contents and deliberate malformed-header case described above.

`scripts/generate-zipx-fixtures.py --seven-zip <reference-7za>` obtains Deflate64, BZip2, LZMA and PPMd payloads from official 7-Zip 26.06 and XZ from Python/liblzma. The owned wrapper fixes names, DOS dates, flags, physical offsets and optional signed descriptors; every final file is read by 7-Zip before writing. The author's [Extra asset](https://github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases/tag/26.06) SHA-256 is `396c180f12d2247c24b0b1fcd482c6fc2a2700f61211ffede1061dd971f5e104`, with bootstrap `7zr.exe` SHA-256 `e80db2dad715a6c5adabe292d31ed54e11f4e9b99ca349827b50573b175891bc`. PPMd inputs test explicit unsupported-method admission; their presence does not declare a decoder. The mixed input contains four compressed records with the same name and a fifth Store record with different bytes. `--check` verifies deterministic reconstruction.

`scripts/generate-lz4-fixtures.py --lz4 <reference-lz4>` uses official LZ4 1.11.1 to create and independently decode standard frames, raw/compressed blocks, linked history, checksums, concatenation and skippable metadata. Legacy and skippable-only vectors test the declared unsupported profiles. The [author Windows x64 ZIP](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/releases/tag/v1.11.1) has SHA-256 `60eb63e00f83fc9613f16cc05cb198f91b41acf903e9092e98b4a7de9ac9783b`. The generator defines all owned byte patterns and verifies exact output before writing; `--check` compares deterministic reconstruction. `lz4-xxh32.bin` contains twelve little-endian `(input_length: u32, xxh32: u32)` records for the existing `(i * 73 ^ (i >> 8)) & 255` pattern, using complete author-generated frame content checksums as the oracle.

`scripts/generate-zstd-fixtures.py --xxhash-reference <owned-reference-wrapper>` uses Python 3.15.1's independent Zstandard 1.5.7 binding. It independently decompresses every generated sample before writing and supports `--check`. Samples cover the owned phrase, empty input, 200000 zero bytes, the script's fixed xorshift/weighted-alphabet pattern of 700000 bytes at four levels, 10000 phrase repetitions, optional checks/size, concatenation/skippable metadata and the existing good/damaged TAR patterns. Their presence does not declare an implemented product decoder. `zstd-xxh64.bin` stores eighteen little-endian `(input_length: u32, xxh64: u64)` records for `(i * 73 ^ (i >> 8)) & 255`, including stripe and tail boundaries through 65536 bytes. Complete 64-bit digests come from the owned [test-only C wrapper](xxhash64-reference.c) calling `XXH64` in the author's header from [Zstandard 1.5.7 source](https://github.com/meta/zstd/releases/tag/v1.5.7), verified before extraction against its official `.sha256` value `eb33e51f49a15e023950cd7825ca74a4a2b43db8354825ac24fc1b7ee09e6fa3`. This wrapper prints the length and hexadecimal digest for lengths 0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 255, 4096 and 65536. Reference sources, wrappers and executables remain under local `build/toolchain/`.

Compile the wrapper with only the verified source's `lib/common` as an include directory, for example `cl /O2 /std:c11 /Ibuild/toolchain/references/zstd-1.5.7/source/zstd-1.5.7/lib/common /Febuild/toolchain/references/zstd-1.5.7/xxh64-vectors.exe /Fobuild/toolchain/references/zstd-1.5.7/xxh64-vectors.obj tests/fixtures/streams/xxhash64-reference.c`. This explicit oracle build is separate from all product build targets.
